item.title: Sweden election: A turning point for the far right?
item.description: The stakes are high in Sweden's general election, with the far right poised to enter government for the first time. TV4 News journalist Markus Karlsson-Bourrioux explains how opinion polls shifted from a comfortable centre-left lead to a tight race over the summer, and how far-right ideas have gained ground since the last election in 2022. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: Thousands rally against far-right after AfD victory
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched in around 20 cities across Germany to protest the rise of the far right after the AfD's historic victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Demonstrators said they were defending democracy as mainstream parties continue to rule out governing with the AfD. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘This is our home’: German minorities defy far-right AfD’s culture of fear after election win
item.description: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt has sent shockwaves through Germany and Europe as far-right parties continue to rise across the continent. Intense hostility has left migrants and minorities in fear of attacks and abuse, Alex Croft reports Fuente: The Independent - World.

item.title: Voting under way in Sweden election that could see far right in government
item.description: Latest poll shows 0.3-point gap between left and right blocs, with country’s reputation as global champion of human rights said to be at stake Sweden goes to the polls on Sunday in an extremely close election that could see the far right enter government for the first time if the country’s rightwing parties can form a majority. Opinion polls show the centre-left opposition alliance ahead, with Magdalena ⁠Andersson of the Social Democrats the favourite to become prime minister again after four years in opposition, but her bloc’s lead has narrowed considerably in the final days of the campaign… Publicado también por: The Guardian - World. item.title: Chinese leader pledges to help Brics nations with AI and smart manufacturing
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped up his one-day trip to India on Sunday, calling for unity among Brics members to counter power politics and pledging to help them develop open-source AI and set up smart manufacturing factories. Speaking at the second day of the Brics summit in New Delhi, he identified these as two out of five key initiatives to promote economic growth and technological development in the Global South. Xi also said Beijing would offer to train young talent from other member... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Swedes vote in close general election that could usher far right into government
item.description: Swedes are heading to the polls Sunday for a general election that will either bring a far right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long been known for. The centre-left opposition holds a narrow lead over the ruling right-wing bloc but Prime ⁠Minister Ulf Kristersson's four-party alliance – which includes the far right Sweden Democrats – has been catching up in the final weeks of campaigning. Publicado también por: The Jerusalem Post - International. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Mass protests erupt in Germany as AfD eyes breakthrough in eastern states
item.description: A massive turnout in Erfurt, Germany saw protesters actively blocking access to the AfD's annual conference, showcasing a strong opposition to the far-right party's agenda. The AfD's lead in national opinion polls and its upcoming eastern state election objectives raise alarms over its increasing power. Mainstream parties continue to adopt a strategy of isolation, refusing to collaborate with the AfD as tensions escalate. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: About 150,000 demonstrators took to the streets in around 20 cities across Germany on Saturday against the far-right AfD, after the party scored a crushing victory in a state election last week. The Alternative for Germany (AfD) topped the vote in the eastern region of Saxony-Anhalt, and is now seeking to form the first extreme-right state government in Germany since World War II. item.title: El presidente de Líbano aboga por la retirada de Israel en una visita sorpresa al sur del país
item.description: La visita inesperada de Joseph Aoun es la primera desde que estalló la guerra con Israel y ocurre tras la destrucción por parte de Israel de una red de túneles de Hezbolá en la estratégica colina de Ali al-Taher. Sin aviso y rodeado de seguridad, Aoun se comprometió a lograr la retirada israelí y a reconstruir la zona. Esto ocurre mientras Israel insiste en que no abandonará las zonas que ocupa en sur libanés y con los diálogos patrocinados por EE. UU. pospuestos hasta octubre. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Tens of thousands protest against far-right AfD party in Germany
item.description: About 150,000 demonstrators took to the streets in around 20 cities across Germany on Saturday against the far-right AfD, after the party scored a crushing victory in a state election last week. The Alternative for Germany (AfD) topped the vote in the eastern region of Saxony-Anhalt, and is now seeking to form the first extreme-right state government in Germany since World War II. item.title: Trump Says Irish Unification Would Be ‘Fantastic,’ Breaking With Precedent
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would “love to see” a united Ireland, wading into a politically sensitive subject as he embarked on a two-day Irish visit that blurs the lines between his presidency and personal business interests. After meeting Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheal Martin in Dublin, Trump said reunification of the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland – split for over a century – would be “a fantastic thing”. “The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. item.title: Will Malaysia’s Umno pull the plug on coalition partner PH?
item.description: The political impasse in Malaysia’s government has regressed to a game of chicken, experts say, with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and the former ruling Umno party trading barbs and dares as pressure grows for snap polls with more than a year left to term. Relations between Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition and erstwhile rivals Umno have hit its lowest point since the two sides cut a deal to form a unity government in 2022, after a series of recent state polls that saw PH all but decimated... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Trump señala que sería «fantástica» la unificación de Irlanda: «No quiero causar ningún problema, pero me encantaría»
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha señalado este sábado que le «encantaría» la unificación de Irlanda, incidiendo en que Reino Unido tendría «algo que decir» pero recalcado que sería «algo fantástico».«No quiero causar ningún problema, pero te diré que me encantaría verlo unificado. item.title: Under Trump’s shadow, Brics takes step towards de-dollarisation
item.description: Brics countries agreed on Saturday to expand trade and payments in local currencies, making another step towards de-dollarisation as the bloc seeks to counter an assertive United States. Facing pressure from Washington, the member nations found enough common ground to overcome some of their biggest diplomatic splits. The pledges were part of the “New Delhi Declaration 2026”, adopted unanimously on the opening day of the 18th Brics summit. After a closed session, Indian Prime Minister Narendra... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
item.description: US president say on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’ • Trump’s visit to Ireland – live updates Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”. The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Washington Post - World. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Xi tells Modi China and India bear ‘significant responsibilities’ as Global South powers
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday that China and India, as the world’s most populous nations and key members of the Global South, bore “significant responsibilities” in an international landscape “fraught with turbulence and change”. That message framed why the two sides should work together despite their differences. Xi said that although the countries had different national circumstances, “there is ample scope for us to learn from each other’s... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: En directo: Irak confirma origen del ataque que obligó a cerrar un oleoducto clave en Arabia Saudita
item.description: Aunque las milicias proiraníes en Irak negaron su involucramiento en el ataque, el Gobierno iraquí aseguró que drones lanzados desde su territorio dañaron el estratégico oleoducto saudita Este-Oeste y prometieron investigar lo ocurrido. Arabia Saudita informó el cierre por precaución de las instalaciones luego de varios ataques registrados la semana pasada y el presidente Donald Trump consideró "probable" que Irán haya estado detrás de la ofensiva. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
